title: The Risk of Going Back to Old Habits — 2 Peter 2:22
paragraphs: The Risk of Going Back to Old Habits — 2 Peter 2:22

You washed the outside.
But the old appetite is still whispering.

“That dog returns to its vomit…”
Peter did not choose soft words. He chose a mirror.
“And a sow, after washing herself, returns to wallow in the mire” (2 Peter 2:22).
This is the danger of going back.

Not just making a mistake.
Not just stumbling in weakness.
But turning back to the very chains Jesus called you out of.

Old habits never come back wearing warning labels.
They come back dressed like comfort.
Like nostalgia.
Like relief.
Like “just this once.”
But sin never stays small. It always wants the throne.

Going back is not only about behavior.
It is about desire.
The hands follow what the heart secretly still worships.
That is why behavior management alone cannot save a soul.
You can wash a pig. You cannot change its nature.
Only Christ can do that.

Jesus did not die just to make you look clean.
He died and rose again to make you new.
New heart. New hunger. New direction.
The Gospel is not God saying, “Try harder not to go back.”
The Gospel is God saying, “Come to My Son and be transformed.”

So if you feel the pull of old habits today, do not flirt with them.
Expose them.
Confess them.
Kill them at the cross.
Run to the One who does not just clean the stain—but breaks the slavery.

You are not called to recycle your old life.
You are called to bury it with Christ.

There is hope.
Even for the one who feels the mud still calling.
Even for the one ashamed of how familiar the vomit looks.
Grace is still stronger.
Repentance is still open.
And Jesus still receives sinners who are ready to come home for real.

Don’t go back to what almost destroyed you.
The cross was too costly.
Your calling is too holy.
And Christ is too good.
